drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 58-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.82, creatinine 1.07-1.11, hemoglobin 14.3-14.5, platelets 223-229, sodium 128-131, wbc 8.5-9.1; vitals dbp 74-79, heart_rate 79-83, map 89-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 117-122, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Fluid restriction 1.2 L/day; Sodium chloride 1 g PO TID
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.07-1.11, hemoglobin 14.2-14.4, platelets 220-231, sodium 131-133, wbc 8.4-9.1; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 79-85, map 90-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-18, sbp 116-122, spo2 97-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 58-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
